absent: Ring folio allocation, user mapping, capacity derivation, and event object layout.
Context allocation and teardown internals including table management and dead marking.
Request credit accounting limits and helpers that add or test availability.
Submission path for read, write, fsync, and poll including control-block parsing.
Fsync request initialization, credential capture, file handling, and work scheduling.
Timer sleeper setup, waitqueue internals, and wakeup ordering beyond use sites.
Security permission and notify backend behavior beyond the permission wrappers.
Error code and flag numeric ABI values and user ring header layout.

findings.text: Provides creation of an asynchronous IO context from a requested event capacity and a user pointer for the resulting identifier. It rejects nonzero prior identifier content and zero capacity, allocates internal state, publishes the new identifier to user space, tears down the allocation when publication fails, and releases the initial user reference.

Provides the 32-bit compatibility variant of context creation with the same validation and lifecycle, differing only by writing the identifier through a narrowed user pointer with truncation treated as safe because the value is an address.

Provides destruction of a context looked up from an identifier. On success it initiates teardown with a one-shot completion waiter, drops the lookup reference, and blocks until outstanding IO drains so user buffers are no longer accessed; unknown identifiers are reported as invalid.
Exposes a helper that drops a reference on an eventfd context and frees it through the reference-count release path when the last reference goes away.
Defines a waiter pairing a generic wait queue entry with a minimum event count threshold used to decide when the sleeper becomes eligible for wakeup.

Context lookup interprets the supplied identifier as a user ring address to fetch a table index, uses RCU protection for table and slot access with speculation hardening of the index, verifies that the stored user identifier matches, and acquires a live user reference only on match.

Request acquisition allocates from a dedicated cache, reclaims completion credits through a user-ring refill attempt when none are immediately available, and on success takes a context request reference, links the new request to the context, initializes list membership and a two-count reference, and clears the event notification handle; allocation or credit failure returns no request and frees any partial allocation.

Request teardown releases an optional event notification handle and file reference, drops the context request reference, and returns the object to its cache. The put path triggers completion exactly once when the reference count reaches zero and then destroys the object, after which the request must not be touched.

Completion publishes one result into a shared ring at an offset following the current tail with wrap at capacity, makes the entry visible before advancing the shared tail, refreshes cached head and tail views, counts the completion, opportunistically returns credits once more than one completion is outstanding, derives current occupancy from head and tail, signals an optional event notification, orders the tail publication against waiter inspection, and wakes plus detaches every waiter whose threshold is satisfied.

Tail update, completed count, and occupancy derivation are protected by the context completion lock in interrupt-disabling mode, allowing completion from interrupt context while excluding concurrent tail writers and head reclaim.

Credit refill treats the shared head as untrusted and reduces it modulo capacity, computes ring occupancy from head and tail order, caps reclaimable completions by occupancy so an invalid head cannot over-credit, and returns with no change when nothing is reclaimable.

User-ring reclaim samples shared head and cached tail while holding the completion lock in interrupt-disabling mode, which blocks concurrent tail advancement and makes either a stale or fresh head value safe when combined with the completed-count check.

Event draining serializes access to the ring folio table and shared head and tail indices with the context ring mutex, which may sleep, and issues a read barrier after sampling the tail so entries up to the tail become visible.

Draining normalizes both indices modulo capacity, stops when empty, copies to user space in chunks bounded by remaining request, contiguous availability, and page remainder, fails the whole call on copy fault, and otherwise advances and publishes the shared head with cache maintenance.

Event waiting first attempts an immediate drain and returns when no deadline applies, on error, or when the minimum is met. Otherwise it arms a monotonic relative timer unless the deadline is infinite, registers an interruptible waiter with a residual threshold, rechecks for new events after each wait preparation, sleeps only when no progress occurred, then unregisters the waiter and cancels the timer.
A read that observes the context marked dead reports invalid, and a read producing no events propagates the underlying negative status rather than zero.
Removal of a request from the context active list is serialized by the context lock in interrupt-disabling mode.

Read and write completion removes the request from the active list when still linked, ends filesystem freeze protection for regular-file writes, records the operation status with a cleared secondary status, and drops the final request reference.

Submission takes filesystem freeze protection for regular-file writes and logically transfers it away from the submitter for lock tracking, while completion reacquires the tracking and then ends the protection, keeping the hold across the asynchronous operation.

Read and write preparation clears streaming hints and private state, sets position from the control block, derives base flags from the file plus an async marker, optionally enables event notification and applies a caller priority after a capability check, inherits current priority otherwise, validates extended read and write flags, and clears the high-priority polling hint.

Extended flag validation rejects unknown bits and mutually exclusive append controls, requires file mode support for nonblocking behavior, restricts atomic behavior to writes on capable files, requires filesystem operation support and excludes DAX mappings for dontcache behavior, merges supported bits, maps synchronous behavior to a data-sync marker, and permits clearing append mode only when the inode is not mandatorily append-only.

Buffer setup imports plain buffers as a single user region and vectored buffers through a vector import path with inline fast storage and compatibility handling, leaving no vector allocation in the plain case.

Dispatch completion leaves queued operations pending for later callback, converts restart-style failures to an interrupt failure before completing, and completes all other statuses through the request completion handler.

Read dispatch validates preparation, read mode, and read iteration support before importing buffers, verifying the area, and invoking the file read path. Write dispatch mirrors this for write mode and write iteration support, adding freeze acquisition for regular files and marking the request as a write before invoking the file write path. Both release any imported vectors afterward.

Area verification rejects negative byte counts, checks for negative positions and position plus length wrap with an exception for files advertising unsigned offsets, then applies security permission and file-area notification permission checks for the access direction.

File-area permission asserts that freeze protection is not held for regular files, ignores masks without access types, optionally emits a pre-content notification for hierarchical-storage modes, then only for read permission with access-permission notification enabled emits a legacy access-permission event. Disabled builds unconditionally allow, and mode selection is governed by alternate macro definitions for notify versus non-notify configurations.

Parent notification resolves the inode from the dentry, returns early when the filesystem has no watchers, tags directory events and bypasses parent handling when the directory name is unwatched, bypasses parent handling for root entries, and otherwise delegates to a parent helper or falls back to child-only notification. The path wrapper forwards to the parent path with path-type data.

Filesystem sync runs in workqueue context under the saved credentials captured at submission, records the sync outcome in the request result, releases the saved credential, and drops the request reference to drive completion.

Because user space can modify the shared head concurrently, reclaim must clamp it into range and limit credit return by both ring occupancy and outstanding completions; omitting either bound risks returning credits for events still visible to the user.

The ring mutex can sleep after the waiter has entered interruptible state and then return to running state, so an empty ring combined with mutex contention can spin through repeated prepare and drain cycles.
Destroy must wait for in-flight operations after initiating teardown; returning early would leave the kernel accessing user buffers after the caller believes the context is gone.
